elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience during the committed term.
elements.evidence: Section IV expressly permits Licensee to terminate the Agreement for convenience, in whole or in part, without limiting that right during the 36-month Initial Period.

elements.element: Customer's termination for convenience may become effective upon 30 days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: Section IV requires thirty (30) days' prior notice.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice must be written.
elements.evidence: Section IV expressly requires prior written notice to Licensor.

elements.element: Vendor must provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees attributable to the period after the effective termination date.
elements.evidence: Section IV requires Licensor to refund any prepaid fees covering the period after the effective date of termination, which operatively provides the required unearned-fee refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Neither the original language nor added Section IV grants Licensor a convenience-termination right. Licensor's immediate termination right is expressly triggered by Licensee breach, not convenience; its unilateral renewal option does not permit mid-term termination.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section IV expressly grants Licensee a termination-for-convenience right without excluding the Initial Period.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice period must be between 60 and 90 days.
elements.evidence: Section IV specifies thirty (30) days' prior notice, which is outside the fallback range of 60–90 days.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee charged to Customer must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: Section IV provides that termination is without penalty, early termination charge, or other liability. A zero early-termination fee is below the three-month cap.

elements.element: If Vendor has a termination-for-convenience right, it may be exercised only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The condition is absent: Licensor has no termination-for-convenience right. Its express termination right is for Licensee breach, while its renewal option is not a termination right.

elements.element: If Vendor has a termination-for-convenience right, it must provide 90 days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: The condition is absent because the Agreement grants Licensor no termination-for-convenience right; therefore, there is no noncompliant Vendor convenience right exercisable on shorter notice.

result.reason: The operative language fully satisfies the preferred position: Licensee receives a 30-day written-notice convenience right, an unearned prepaid-fee refund, and Licensor receives no corresponding convenience right during the term. The fallback is not independently satisfied because its required 60–90-day Customer notice period is not present. The amendment is not minimal because it additionally permits partial termination and adds broad 'other liability' language beyond what is necessary for the preferred position. The drafting generally preserves unrelated terms, but partial termination lacks scope and fee-adjustment mechanics, and 'other liability' is potentially overbroad.
